claims.claim: The CLI exposes run, check, list, coverage and index.

claims.claim: docs/measurement.md's per-repo table sums to its own stated totals: 16 repositories, 553 claims checked, 98 contradicted, 33 unsupported, 131 defective (24%).
claims.metric: the table's rows summed and compared with the total row, in the document itself
claims.method: the audit's per-repo verdicts were recorded per batch; this keeps the report's arithmetic honest if either the rows or the totals are edited

check.cmd: python3 -c "import re,pathlib;t=pathlib.Path('docs/measurement.md').read_text();rows=[r for r in re.findall(r'^\|\s*([^|*]+?)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|\s*(\d+)\s*\|', t, re.M)];tot=re.findall(r'^\|\s*\*\*(\d+) repositories\*\*\s*\|\s*\*\*(\d+)\*\*\s*\|\s*\*\*(\d+)\*\*\s*\|\s*\*\*(\d+)\*\*\s*\|', t, re.M)[0];s=[len(rows)]+[sum(int(r[i]) for r in rows) for i in (1,2,3)];d=s[2]+s[3];pct=round(100*d/s[1]);print('sums', *s, d, '| stated', *[int(x) for x in tot], int(tot[2])+int(tot[3]), '| pct', pct, '| doc says 24%:', '24%' in t)"

claims.claim: `coverage` lists the README numbers no claim mentions and always exits 0 — it is a to-do list, not a gate. Its own report on this README leads with the illustration numbers from the worked example, and the gate still passes.
claims.metric: exit code of `coverage`, and whether it prints candidates
claims.method: the command scans this README, prints every number no claim mentions, and returns 0; only `run` decides pass/fail

claims.claim: Across the 22 repositories this tool guards, `coverage` found 176 number-like mentions matched by a claim and 78 that no claim mentions — an upper bound on unclaimed work, not a defect count.
claims.metric: unclaimed candidates reported by `coverage --max 0` over the 22 guarded repositories
claims.method: run 2026-09-14 against local clones of all 22 repositories, once for each; the figure moves as READMEs and claims change, and the remaining candidates are dominated by numbers that are not figures at all (example sizes, HTTP codes, CSS percentages, dates) plus numbers written as words, which the scan cannot see in either direction
claims.repro: for d in <the 22 clones>; do python3 -m verify_claims --root ../$d coverage --max 0; done

claims.metric: rows/claims/machine/manual parsed back out of the committed page
claims.method: `index_page.summarise` re-reads the rendered page: total must equal machine + manual, and the page must still carry the do-not-edit notice
claims.repro: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "from verify_claims import index_page as i; print(i.summarise(open('docs/index.md').read()))"

check.cmd: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "from verify_claims import index_page as i;t=open('docs/index.md').read();r,tot,m,man=i.summarise(t);assert tot==m+man,(tot,m,man);assert r>0;assert 'do not edit by hand' in t;print('consistent',r,tot,m,man)"

claims.claim: Every path the repository-root `llms.txt` points at exists in the repository, and every https link it publishes is on this project's own domain or a known host.
claims.value: every local path in llms.txt exists
claims.metric: relative paths named in llms.txt vs the files on disk; hosts of its absolute links
claims.method: parses llms.txt, resolves each github.com/alloevil/verify-claims/blob/main/<path> target against the working tree, and requires each to exist — the file is prose for answer engines, so a link to a renamed document would otherwise rot unnoticed

check.cmd:
python3 -c "import re, pathlib
t = pathlib.Path('llms.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
bt = chr(96)
targets = set(re.findall(r'blob/main/([^\s)]+)', t))
targets |= set(re.findall(bt + r'([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(?:md|json|yml|txt))' + bt, t))
missing = sorted(p for p in targets if not pathlib.Path(p).exists())
print('targets', len(targets), 'missing', missing)
assert targets and not missing"

claims.claim: Every page or SVG in this repository that animates also handles `prefers-reduced-motion` — motion here is decoration, and the artefact must stay complete when it is off.
claims.value: no animated file without a reduced-motion branch
claims.metric: files containing an animation primitive vs files containing `prefers-reduced-motion`
claims.method: the check walks every committed page and SVG and covers all four ways one can move — CSS animations/keyframes, SVG SMIL, requestAnimationFrame, and the CSS animations inside an SVG hero — requiring a `prefers-reduced-motion` reference wherever it finds one. SVG heroes are included because GitHub renders them through : scripts do not run, CSS animations do, and a hero that loops forever is exactly what a reduced-motion branch is for.

check.cmd:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re

MOVES = re.compile(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes|<animate\b|<animateTransform\b|requestAnimationFrame')
RELAX = 'prefers-reduced-motion'
pages = sorted(set(
    list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('*.html'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('docs/*.html'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('assets/*.svg'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('assets/readme/*.svg'))
))
pages = [p for p in pages if p.name != 'template.html']
animated, missing = 0, []
for p in pages:
    t = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if MOVES.search(t):
        animated += 1
        if RELAX not in t:
            missing.append(str(p))
print('files', len(pages), 'animated', animated, 'missing', missing)
assert animated and not missing
PY
